output.summary: The run is VALID but the overall policy verdict is NO_VERDICT and analysis coverage is INCOMPLETE (RESOURCE_GAPS, MISSING_RESOURCE_CELLS). Workload-03 (target 90 rps) passed latency (p95 53ms vs 200ms threshold) but FAILed compute-limit (cpu_work mean 0.9004095233 > 0.9 threshold) and database-limit was NO_VERDICT because one db_work cell is missing, so the window verdict is NO_VERDICT. Workload-04 (target 110 rps) shows a severe regression: cpu_work near 1.0 across all 300 cells (mean 0.99997633, max 1), compute-limit FAIL, and latency p95 28815ms against the 200ms threshold (latency FAIL), so the window verdict is FAIL. db_work stayed low (~0.02496 mean, max 0.026069) and its 0.9-limit PASSed in workload-04. Recorded error_count is 0 in both windows. The correlation analysis did not establish a CPU-to-latency link (statuses BELOW_EFFECT/INSUFFICIENT_DATA, uncertainty NOT_ESTIMATED for every pair, headline selection UNAVAILABLE for all four pairs), anomalies_tested is 0, and clock alignment is not_verified_by_core, so the coincident CPU saturation and latency regression are hypotheses to test, not proven causes.

hypotheses.observation: In workload-04 (1704068100000–1704068400000, target 110 rps) cpu_work averaged 0.99997633 with max 1.0 and min 0.992899, the compute-limit check (threshold 0.9) is FAIL with a single finding covering all 300 cells, and response_time_p95 was 28815ms against the 200ms threshold (latency FAIL). In workload-03 (target 90 rps) cpu_work averaged 0.9004095233 and p95 latency was 53ms with latency PASS.
hypotheses.possible_explanation: The increase from ~90 rps to ~110 rps coincides with CPU utilization pinned near 1.0 and multi-second latencies, suggesting the system is at or beyond CPU capacity at the higher load and requests queue instead of failing.
hypotheses.recommended_check: Verify clock alignment, then re-run with a gradual load ramp while recording CPU saturation and queueing telemetry (thread pool depth, run queue, time-in-queue vs service time) to test whether throughput near CPU capacity drives the latency increase.

hypotheses.observation: In workload-04, error_count is 0 and error_rate_ratio is 0/33000 while p50 latency was 15231ms, p95 28815ms and max 30323ms; the recorded throughput is 33000000/300000 = 110 rps, equal to the 110 rps target rate.
hypotheses.possible_explanation: Requests appear to eventually complete (recorded throughput matches target) but with very high latency, consistent with deep queuing or head-of-line blocking under saturation rather than immediate failures.
hypotheses.recommended_check: Confirm whether timed-out or discarded requests are excluded from error_count, and measure in-flight concurrency and queue depth during a repeat of the 110 rps step to test the queuing hypothesis.

hypotheses.observation: In workload-04, db_work averaged 0.02496306 with max 0.026069, the database-limit check (threshold 0.9) is PASS, and the db_work-to-latency correlation status is BELOW_EFFECT; in workload-03 db_work averaged 0.0224960769.
hypotheses.possible_explanation: Database utilization is far below the 0.9 limit in both windows, so the database is unlikely to be the primary bottleneck in the observed latency regression; however db_work may not capture every aspect of database pressure.
hypotheses.recommended_check: Verify what the db_work metric measures (engine utilization vs connection/wait/queue pools) and inspect database-side wait and pool metrics during a repeat run before excluding the database from the regression.

hypotheses.observation: In workload-03, db_work has missing_cells=1 with reason RESOURCE_GAPS, the database-limit check returned NO_VERDICT with reason MISSING_RESOURCE_CELLS, and analysis coverage is INCOMPLETE (RESOURCE_GAPS, MISSING_RESOURCE_CELLS).
hypotheses.possible_explanation: A single missing db_work cell prevented a database-limit verdict in workload-03; the gap may be a collection artifact rather than a service event, but that cannot be assumed from the data present.
hypotheses.recommended_check: Locate and explain the missing db_work cell in workload-03 (or re-collect/re-run that window) so the database-limit policy can be evaluated and full coverage restored.

hypotheses.observation: The CPU-to-latency association was not established: workload-03 association-01 has status BELOW_EFFECT (raw_rho 0.446860229552, control target-request-rate dropped as CONSTANT_CONTROL, uncertainty NOT_ESTIMATED), workload-04 association-01 has status INSUFFICIENT_DATA (NO_RESIDUAL_VARIATION, LAG_NOT_EVALUABLE), and headline selection is UNAVAILABLE for all four pairs (MULTI_WINDOW_FAMILY_UNSUPPORTED, with GENUINE_PARTIAL_UNCALIBRATED on the workload-04 pairs).
hypotheses.possible_explanation: The current analysis cannot statistically link CPU usage to the latency regression: associations are below effect or unevaluable, no p-values exist, and the partial correlation is uncalibrated, so CPU saturation is unproven as the cause.
hypotheses.recommended_check: Re-run the correlation with a supported method for the multi-window family that calibrates the partial correlation and yields p-values, and with a non-constant load control, before accepting a CPU-saturation explanation.

hypotheses.recommended_check: Review the compute-limit threshold policy and the interval-mean sampling/aggregation semantics, and assess whether sustained vs marginal exceedances (~0.900–0.931 ratio) are intended to fail the SLA.
